clue.text: Lots of water and wine drinking companion examined

parts.note: a sea is a large body of water

indicators.note: something drinking takes a liquid inside itself, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: red is wine by colour
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A drinker of wine and water is inspected alongside a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The companion sits inside the wine, and the sea goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To have searched something is to have inspected it closely, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Goddess wanting husband for a very long time

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the goddess

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A goddess has been without a husband for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H of HERA to leave ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long historical period, so it serves for a lengthy stretch of time.

clue.text: Are you texting student about returning part of geometry kit?

parts.note: in text-message shorthand 'are you' is written R U
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone messages a pupil asking whether they are returning a borrowed piece of a maths set.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is the straight edge found in a school geometry set alongside compass and protractor.

clue.text: Speculation he shot spy I broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rumour goes out on air that a man shot a spy, as the speaker confesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a supposition or theory not yet proven, so it is a form of conjecture.

clue.text: Sinks blade into rampant knight? On the contrary!

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up on hind legs, and in a down clue rearing up flips the word upwards
into says one piece goes inside another
the exclamation swaps the roles the surface gave, so the thing said to go inside becomes the outside

parts.note: a sword is a blade
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: Someone plunges a blade into a rearing heraldic knight, then insists it was the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' reverses the surface instruction: the knight goes into the upturned blade, not the blade into the knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowns as a verb means submerges or goes under, matching the third-person verb sinks.

clue.text: Row after sailor died on a ship

indicators.note: after places the word for row behind the sailor in the finished string

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
to row is to oar a boat
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An argument broke out after a seaman died at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' wants to be a quarrel; it is the verb of propelling a boat. The oar comes after the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard is the adverb for being on or in a vessel, a direct equivalent.

clue.text: Degenerates set up video game company

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means placed upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Sega is the Japanese video game maker

explanation.surface: Delinquents establish a computer gaming firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to decline with time, so ages works as the verb degenerates.

clue.text: Playing hearts or clubs before players

indicators.note: playing with letters means rearranging them for fun

parts.note: taken as written
C is clubs in card notation

explanation.surface: A card player chooses between leading hearts or clubs ahead of the other players.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture misleads: 'Playing' signals the shuffle and 'players' are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of instrumental musicians, so it is a group of players.

clue.text: Celebrating two bands receiving Eastern gong

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the two bands hold the rest within them

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band, and a ring is a band of metal
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
gong is slang for a medal or honour, and the MBE is a British one

explanation.surface: Two musical groups toast receiving a gong from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for an honour such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: Remembering an event can mean commemorating it, as in remembering the fallen.

clue.text: Career Republicans pocketing the lot

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the GOP (Grand Old Party) is the US Republican Party
the lot means everything

explanation.surface: Republican politicians make a career of grabbing everything for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is not a profession here but the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash at speed, and to gallop is likewise to run fast.

clue.text: Break past Coe, keeping close to Cram

parts.note: over means finished or past

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the runner's name holds a letter inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe breaks away while Steve Cram stays close behind him in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Coe and Cram were rival British middle-distance runners of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome resistance or a person is to break them, defeating them utterly.

clue.text: Talking about sport and running

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech word goes around the sport

parts.note: orating is speaking formally
PE is physical education, school sport

explanation.surface: Someone chats about games and jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport and running' look like a pair of pastimes; running is the definition, as in a machine running.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is working or functioning, which is what running means here.

clue.text: Relative shares reason for travelling to prison

parts.note: a pro, as in pros and cons, is an argument in favour

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they are making the trip to visit a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason for travelling' looks like one phrase; the split is after 'for', with 'travelling' acting on what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportions are parts considered in relation to a whole, that is comparative amounts.

clue.text: Appears to be writing on diocese

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another sits after it, so the writing comes second

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: It looks like a written piece about a church district.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the writing follows the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Seems is a verb meaning gives the impression of being, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Divisive chairs accepting reduced role

indicators.note: accepting means letting in, so the seats take a word inside

parts.note: seating is chairs collectively

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Committee chairmen at odds take on a lesser role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairs' looks like people chairing meetings; it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something separating forces groups apart, so it causes division between them.

clue.text: Respected alumnus spotted

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
eyed means looked at, caught sight of

explanation.surface: A distinguished former student is seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respected' looks like an adjective praising the alumnus but is the verb heeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected rules are complied with, so obeyed fits as a past-tense verb of compliance.

clue.text: Bigoted vice-president initially ignored reality

indicators.note: the first letter of each is left out, as if passed over at the start

parts.note: a sexist is prejudiced on grounds of sex
Mike Pence was US vice-president under Trump

explanation.surface: A prejudiced deputy leader overlooked the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is the state of being real, so it serves as a synonym for actuality.

clue.text: Moderate bit of inheritance covers time left

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so the inherited unit surrounds two letters

parts.note: a gene is a unit of heredity
T is time
L is left

explanation.surface: A small legacy pays for the remaining period, within reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of inheritance' suggests money from a will; it is a gene.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle as an adjective means mild or not extreme, the same as moderate.

clue.text: Ring doctor during birth

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to doctor results is to rig them
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a physician while a baby is being born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring doctor' reads as phoning a medic; doctor is the verb meaning falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth can mean beginnings or descent, as in noble birth, which is what origin means.

clue.text: Island fruit, oddly acidic

parts.note: a haw is the berry of the hawthorn

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions only, the first, third and so on

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Tropical fruit from an island tastes strangely sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island fruit' suggests a pineapple; the fruit is the humble hawthorn berry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii is the largest island of the Pacific state that shares its name.

clue.text: Old queen takes her son's ex to my boss

indicators.note: takes means receives into itself, so the royal letters enclose the rest

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
Diana, Princess of Wales, was the former wife of Elizabeth II's son Charles
taken as written

explanation.surface: The late Queen brings her son's former wife to meet the speaker's employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My boss' is the setter speaking: the crossword setter answers to the puzzles editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper setter's work is commissioned and checked by an editor, so the editor is their superior.

clue.text: Figures to the left and to the right

indicators.text: to the left and to the right
indicators.note: a word that reads the same in either direction, leftwards or rightwards, is symmetrical

parts.words: to the left and to the right
parts.note: the word reads identically from either end

explanation.surface: Numbers are laid out on both sides of the page.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is just a description of the answer as a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is short for statistics, which are numerical data.

clue.text: Use commercial vehicle identification badge at last

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a van is a vehicle
a tag is an identifying label

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to deploy a trade vehicle's ID badge at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Identification badge' reads as one item; it splits into a label and the final letter of 'badge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Use as a noun means benefit, as in 'of no use', which is what advantage means.

clue.text: Someone else's son released from jail after ambassador intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the envoy goes inside
released from means let out of, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
S is son
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A boy is freed from prison after a diplomat steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive for belonging to another person or people, a pronoun fit.

clue.text: Go with rising cry

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means going upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating
W is with

explanation.surface: Head off with a mounting wail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' as in needing to go to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to shed tears, so weep is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unknown tongues confused most recent arrival

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The newcomer is bewildered by foreign languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest child of a family is the last-born, the latest addition.

clue.text: Ladies abandoned morals

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so the letters run loose

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Women gave up their principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like a verb, ladies dropping morals; it is the adjective meaning unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or standards of conduct, so they are a person's moral values.

clue.text: Contents of stranger story

indicators.note: the contents of something are what is inside it, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: a stranger is an alien; its inside letters are kept

explanation.surface: The substance of an odder tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranger is the noun, an alien, not the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can mean a fib, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Met founder reversing when in the van, not paying attention

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the founder's name is read right to left

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel founded London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A police founder backs up while a passenger in the van dozes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police. 'In the van' means at the front, so the word for when leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep, or figuratively asleep, is inattentive, as in 'asleep at the wheel'.

clue.text: Watched on, cautious when out of uniform

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: out of means without, so a letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: guarded means wary
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone kept watch, careful when not wearing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of uniform' suggests plain clothes; it means losing the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarded means looked at attentively, so it is a past-tense synonym of watched.
